transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Hello! I'm Dora, your clinical conversational agent. I've just reviewed your follow-up check after cataract surgery. Do you have any questions about your surgery or recovery?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Hi Dora, yes, I do have a few questions. First, I'm wondering when I can start doing a little bit of gardening?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
According to the information, you can start with light exercise, such as gardening, about 1 week after surgery. However, it's also recommended to avoid getting water in your eye for the first month. So, it's best to wear protective eyewear and be careful not to get water in your eyes when gardening. Does that help?

Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Yes, it does help, thank you. My next question is about using eye gel for dry eyes. When can I start using it?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
You should have been prescribed eye drops to help with dryness. According to the information, it's recommended to use preservative-free eye drops four times daily to start. If you're running out, you can contact your GP to get some more. They can also help with any other eye care needs you may have. Does that answer your question?

Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Yes, that makes sense. Another thing I've noticed is that I'm very sensitive to bright light. Is that normal?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.intended:
Some sensitivity to light is normal, especially in the first few weeks after surgery. However, if it's severe or you're experiencing significant pain when it's bright, it's not normal and we may need to assess it further. Mild sensitivity, though, is common, and wearing sunglasses can help. Does that make sense?

Do you have any other questions?
transcript.delivered: Some sensitivity to light is normal, especially in the first few weeks after surgery. However, if it's severe or you're experiencing significant pain when it's bright,

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Oh, actually, I also wanted to ask if it's normal to still have some blurriness by now?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
It's common for vision to not be completely clear in the first week after surgery, but it should improve quickly and settle down over time. If your vision is still blurry or getting significantly worse, we may need to check it to make sure it's okay. It's also worth noting that if you had a standard lens put in, you might need reading glasses or varifocals for reading, which is normal.

Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: No, that's all the questions I had. Thank you for the information, Dora!

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
It was my pleasure to help. I'm glad I could answer your questions about your cataract surgery recovery.

Now, just to confirm: did I answer all your questions to your satisfaction?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Yes, you answered all my questions. Thanks again for the help!
